commit_message:
winch: Simplify the handling of `wasm_load`s (#10012)

This commit aims to simplify how `wasm_load`s are currently handled in
the compiler by reducing the number of invariants that need to be
encoded at callsites which make their emission error prone.

Concretely this change:

* Augments `ExtendKind`, to account for unsigned extends; prior to this
  commit it wasn't explicit which loads required unsigned extends.
* Derive `OperandSize` from `ExtendKind`, removing from the caller the
  responsibility of encoding the operand size to use.

fix_commit.message: Winch: Fix Wasm vector loads to operate on 64-bits (#10127)
fix_commit.author: Jeffrey Charles

findings.title: Winch derives undersized bounds-check operand size for SIMD vector-extend loads
findings.message: The Winch baseline compiler's `LoadKind::derive_operand_size()` computes the `OperandSize` that is passed down into `wasm_load`/`load_impl` to perform the Wasm linear-memory bounds check and emit the actual load instruction. For `LoadKind::VectorExtend(vector)` (used for v128 `load8x8`/`load16x4`/`load32x2` sign/zero-extending SIMD loads), this commit routes the size through the newly added `operand_size_for_vector()` helper, which maps V128Extend8x8{S,U} -> OperandSize::S8, V128Extend16x4{S,U} -> OperandSize::S16, and V128Extend32x2{S,U} -> OperandSize::S32. However, all of these Wasm vector-extend-load instructions actually read 8 bytes (64 bits) from linear memory before widening into 8/16/32-bit lanes of a v128 — e.g. `v128.load32x2_s` reads two 32-bit lanes (8 bytes total), not 4. Because the derived (too-small) OperandSize is what callers use both to size the actual memory access and to validate/bound the access against the heap/guard region, the bounds check and the code emitted for the load are checking/loading fewer bytes (1, 2, or 4) than are truly read (8), allowing the load to read up to 4-7 bytes past the validated/intended bound of linear memory for addresses near the end of the accessible region.
findings.suggestion: Derive the operand size for all `VectorExtendKind` variants as 64 bits (`OperandSize::S64`), since every v128 extend-load (load8x8/load16x4/load32x2, signed or unsigned) reads a full 8-byte quantity from linear memory regardless of the resulting narrow lane width. Remove the per-variant 8/16/32-bit mapping in `operand_size_for_vector` (or delete the helper entirely) and have `derive_operand_size` return `OperandSize::S64` directly for `Self::VectorExtend(_)`, matching how the actual load/bounds-check size is computed.

ground_truth.root_cause: The refactor in #10012 conflated 'bits per source lane before widening' with 'total bytes read from memory' when deriving the OperandSize for vector-extend loads. The derived size is reused for both bounds checking and instruction emission, so an incorrect (too-small) per-lane size was propagated into the memory-safety-relevant bounds computation instead of being independently fixed at 8 bytes (the true width of the SIMD extend-load instructions on x86-64/AArch64).
